title: What is the difference between strategy, operations, technology and implementation consulting?
description: The main types of consulting work explained simply, with examples of the questions each answers and which firms tend to do each.
hook: Strategy consulting decides what an organisation should do; operations consulting makes it run better; technology consulting chooses and builds the systems it runs on; and implementation consulting makes an agreed change actually happen. A strategy team might spend six weeks deciding whether a company should enter India, while an implementation team might spend a year rolling out a new system across 40 countries. Knowing the difference helps you choose which firms and roles to apply for, and how to prepare.
body:
The four types at a glance

TypeCore questionTypical output
StrategyWhat should we do?A recommendation and the case for it
OperationsHow do we do it better?A redesigned process with measured savings
TechnologyWhich systems, and how do we build them?A system choice, design or working platform
ImplementationHow do we make the change stick?Delivered change and tracked results

Strategy consulting: what should we do?

Big direction-setting questions for senior leaders: which markets to enter, whether to buy a company, how to grow, how to respond to a competitor. Projects are often short and intense, a few weeks to a few months, and end with a recommendation to the chief executive or board. This is the work most associated with McKinsey, BCG and Bain, firms such as Oliver Wyman, Kearney and L.E.K., and the strategy arms of larger firms: Monitor Deloitte, Strategy& at PwC and EY-Parthenon. The map of top firms covers who is who.

Operations consulting: how do we do it better?

Making the business faster, cheaper or more reliable: supply chains, procurement, manufacturing, customer service, hospital patient flow. The work is more hands-on, with detailed process data, site visits and time spent with front-line teams. Success is usually measured in hard numbers: cost per unit, defect rates, waiting times.

Technology and digital consulting

Choosing and implementing systems such as cloud platforms, data and AI tools, and cybersecurity, and redesigning how the business works around them. Accenture and the Big Four have very large technology practices, and projects can involve hundreds of people. Some roles are close to strategy (deciding what to build and why); others are close to engineering.

Implementation consulting: making it happen

Strategy work tends to end at the decision. Implementation work continues until the change is delivered and the results show up: planning the roll-out, running pilots, training staff, tracking whether the numbers move. Projects are longer, teams are larger and consultants work side by side with the client's people.

One client problem through four lenses

A bank receives 200,000 online account applications a year, but 40% of applicants abandon the process, so only 120,000 become customers. Each new customer is worth about $150 a year in profit. (These numbers are illustrative.)

  • Strategy asks whether these are customers the bank wants and how it can win them against digital-only rivals. If abandonment fell to 30%, the bank would gain 20,000 customers: 20,000 × $150 = $3M a year. Is that worth chasing compared with other priorities?
  • Operations maps the journey step by step and finds where people drop out, say at identity checks that take two days.
  • Technology evaluates instant identity-verification systems, how they integrate with the bank's core platform and what they cost. A $4M system that delivers the $3M a year pays back in about 1.3 years.
  • Implementation redesigns the process, trains staff, launches in phases and tracks completion rates weekly until the target is hit.

The same problem, four kinds of work. In practice one project often contains several of these, which is why the labels blur.

The lines blur

Most firms do some of everything. Strategy firms increasingly stay on to help implement, and large firms have dedicated strategy teams. What matters for you is the practice, the role and the problems you would work on, not just the firm's name. Read about the specific office's work, speak to consultants in the practice and ask what a first-year consultant actually does there.

Which suits you?

  • Enjoy big, open questions and a fast pace? Look at strategy roles.
  • Enjoy measurable improvements and time on the front line? Look at operations.
  • Enjoy technology and building things? Look at technology consulting.
  • Want to see your work through to results? Look at implementation roles.

How it changes your interview preparation

The core skills are the same everywhere: structure, clean maths and a clear recommendation. Then adjust the lens to the role.

  • Strategy: compare options and market economics, and be ready for market entry, growth and M&A cases.
  • Operations: quantify throughput, bottlenecks and cost per unit. The operations case guide works through one in full.
  • Technology or transformation: add adoption, integration, data and delivery risk to the business case.

Compare two answers to "How would you reduce abandonment?" in a technology interview.

"I'd buy a better identity-check system."
"First I'd find where applicants drop out. If it is the two-day identity check, an instant verification tool is worth testing, but I'd check how it integrates with the core system and pilot it on one product before a full roll-out."

The second diagnoses before it prescribes and thinks about delivery. The best structure follows the client's problem, not the job title.

Practice

A retailer's stock runs out too often. Give one question each type of consultant would ask.

Show the answer

Strategy: are we stocking the right range for the customers we want to win? Operations: where in the supply chain do delays occur, and how accurate are our forecasts? Technology: does our inventory system give stores and warehouses a real-time view of stock? Implementation: how do we roll out a new replenishment process to 300 stores and check it is being followed?
